name: Gazlowe's Ledger
summary: A shipment from Booty Bay is missing, and Gazlowe checks his records against Ratchet's harbor manifest.

sections.title: Ratchet's Commercial Records
sections.body: Gazlowe keeps a personal ledger of trade goods in Ratchet. It records imported crates, outbound cargo, and what is stored in the warehouses. When a shipment from Booty Bay goes missing, he compares the goods he expected with the dock records kept by Wharfmaster Dizzywig.

sections.title: Uncovering the Theft
sections.body: Gazlowe and the other goblins compare the ledger with Dizzywig's harbor logs. The cargo never reached Ratchet's port warehouse, confirming Gazlowe's suspicion that the crates were taken before coming ashore. The Southsea Freebooters along the nearby Merchant Coast are to blame.

faq.answer: Gazlowe's Ledger records goods expected and stored in Ratchet. When a shipment goes missing, Gazlowe sends it to the docks to compare its entries with the wharf records.

faq.q: Who needs to inspect the ledger?
aliases: who do i take the ledger to
faq.answer: Wharfmaster Dizzywig checks Gazlowe's Ledger against his shipping logs. He oversees the Ratchet docks and can tell whether missing goods were misplaced or never unloaded.

faq.q: What cargo was missing in the ledger?
faq.answer: Gazlowe was waiting for his latest shipment from Booty Bay. Dizzywig finds nothing amiss in his logs, though goods from Undermine are waiting for Gazlowe to pick up.

faq.q: What happens after the ledger is checked?
faq.answer: Dizzywig checks whether the shipment passed through the docks. When he finds it did not, the ledger returns to Gazlowe, confirming that Southsea Freebooters likely intercepted the cargo at sea.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you can trade at Ratchet, a neutral port. Help Gazlowe trace stolen shipments and keep good standing with the local Steamwheedle authorities.
As a rogue, you can glimpse the flow of contraband, valuable imports, and piracy along the Barrens coast in a goblin boss's private trade ledger.
